purpose: Determine the useful receptor-pool cardinality by a frozen k=1..6 objective staircase before committing to a hardware-sized QUBO.

k_schedule.rationale: Single receptor baseline; no ensemble redundancy term.
Two-receptor union coverage; a ligand needs one supporting conformation.
Two independent conformations must support an active ligand.
Two-hit consensus with a modest positive-correlation redundancy penalty.
Three-hit consensus prevents a five-member pool from relying on a small subpool.
Three-hit consensus with structural-score diversity for the largest screened pool.

algorithm.decoy_constraint: z_d>=x_i for every selected receptor that exposes decoy d
algorithm.internal_objective: weighted active threshold coverage - decoy_weight*weighted decoy exposure - redundancy_weight*mean positive score correlation
algorithm.external_comparison_metric: same robust composite BEDROC20 for every k: mean of primary, mean seed, and worst seed
algorithm.selection_solver: exact enumeration of every receptor subset at each k with reconstructed feasible auxiliary assignment

stopping_rule.increment_definition: mean outer-holdout robust composite at k minus mean outer-holdout robust composite at k-1
stopping_rule.continue_condition: both targets have positive mean increment and at least five positive folds out of eight
stopping_rule.stop_condition: two consecutive k increments fail the continue condition, or maximum_k is reached
stopping_rule.selection_rule: report the smallest k within one standard error of the best observed mean; do not use a single noisy fold as a stop signal

interpretation_boundary: Stage 20 is a post-hoc train-only cardinality design review over MK14 and PPARG. It adds no docking, reads no fresh-validation, locked-test, or BACE1 rows, and does not demonstrate quantum execution or quantum advantage. Its output is a recommendation for the next preregistered cardinality and objective, not a revised validation claim.
